title: Chance Favours the Prepared Mind
paragraphs: In nineteen twenty eight, the Scottish bacteriologist Alexander Fleming returned from a holiday to find that a mould had contaminated one of his dishes. Instead of throwing the dish away, he noticed that the bacteria near the mould had been destroyed. He concluded that the mould released a substance able to kill bacteria, and he named it penicillin. The dish could easily have been thrown away, and the discovery lost.

Fleming published his findings in nineteen twenty nine, yet for about a decade he treated the substance mainly as a possible antiseptic. Turning penicillin into a usable drug required a different kind of effort. At Oxford University, Howard Florey and Ernst Chain led a team that learned how to produce and test the drug. By nineteen forty, they had shown that it could fight many bacterial diseases.

The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for nineteen forty five was shared by all three men. The story shows that a lucky observation matters only when someone is prepared to notice it and others are willing to finish the work. It also shows how slow and shared scientific progress often is.
